channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: TSE publica acórdão do julgamento de Cláudio Castro, que está inelegível e não foi cassado
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) published the ruling that makes Claudio Castro (PL) ineligible for abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections. The majority of ministers determined that his resignation as governor of Rio de Janeiro was voluntary, not a removal, upholding the eight-year ineligibility penalty.

item.title: Crusoé: Lula sem gás
item.description: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz, resulting from the U.S.-Iran conflict that began in late February, threatens to raise fuel prices in Brazil, adding pressure to President Lula’s (PT) re-election bid. This development further complicates an already challenging economic landscape for his campaign.

item.title: Michelle pressiona família Bolsonaro por apoio a mulheres em postos-chave nas eleições deste ano
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro is pressuring the Bolsonaro family to support female candidacies in key positions for the 2026 elections, advocating for Celina Leão’s nomination for the Federal District governorship and Priscila Costa as vice on Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential ticket. She rejects a merely honorary role in the PL and demands her influence be respected in party decisions, while Flávio has dismissed her complaints, heightening family tensions.

item.title: Crusoé: O que Moraes dizia sobre a sátira de personalidades públicas
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes of the STF had previously stated that satire targeting public figures is legitimate and protected by the Constitution, even when offensive. His remarks resurfaced amid controversy over the animated series 'Os Intocáveis', produced by Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema, which criticizes STF ministers, including Gilmar Mendes, who reportedly objected to the content. The original Antagonista post notes that Moraes views criticism and humor as essential instruments of democratic debate.

item.title: Zema nega uso do Estado para benefício próprio ao se comparar a Flávio e intensifica ataques ao STF
item.description: Romeu Zema denied using the state for personal benefit while comparing himself to Flávio Dino and intensified his criticisms of the Supreme Federal Court (STF). The governor of Minas Gerais attended a meeting convened by Hugo Motta with other governors to discuss the Legal Framework for Combating Organized Crime.

item.title: O pedido de desculpas de Gilmar Mendes após fala homofóbica sobre Zema
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes apologized for a homophobic remark made against pre-candidate Romeu Zema, in which he equated homosexuality with crime. He maintained his criticism of Zema but retracted the offensive statement after backlash. The incident unfolded amid a public feud between the two, sparked by an animated video from Zema depicting Mendes in corrupt acts.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Medida para compensar alta da gasolina indica concessão da Fazenda por estratégia eleitoral
item.description: The federal government presented a bill to Congress to use extra oil revenue to offset cuts in fuel taxes, signaling the economic team's willingness to accommodate Lula's electoral strategy. The measure includes reducing taxes on aviation kerosene, previously resisted by the Finance Ministry, highlighting a shift toward electoral pragmatism over fiscal orthodoxy.

item.title: Médico afirma que lesão de pele de Lula é ‘comum’ e sem risco
item.description: Doctor Roberto Kalil Filho stated that the skin lesion removed from President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's head is the most common in the world and poses no risk of metastasis. Lula is expected to be discharged soon, without needing medication or facing restrictions, and will be able to resume normal activities, including his October re-election campaign.

item.title: Kalil anuncia cirurgia ‘sem intercorrência’ e prevê alta de Lula nesta sexta
item.description: Cardiologist Roberto Kalil announced that President Lula underwent medical procedures at Sírio-Libanés Hospital on Friday, including removal of a scalp keratosis and a wrist infiltration for right thumb tendonitis, without complications. Discharge is expected today, though he is advised to avoid large events in the coming days. Lula will need to wear a dressing and hat for about a month due to a sun-exposed scalp lesion, but this should not disrupt his schedule.

item.title: Procedimentos correram bem e não devem afetar campanha de Lula, relata equipe médica
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was treated at Sírio-Libanês Hospital for removal of a skin lesion (basal cell carcinoma) and a biopsy of scalp actinic keratosis. The procedures occurred without complications and are not expected to affect his electoral campaign, with discharge expected by noon and resumption of activities in about two days.

item.title: Espero que Senado tenha coragem, diz Zema sobre impeachment de Gilmar
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and presidential pre-candidate, said he hopes the Senate will have the courage to proceed with the impeachment of Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes, criticizing the Court for becoming a source of conflict and negotiations. He labeled the STF the 'great cause of conflict' in Brazil and accused justices of using their positions for enrichment, calling Alexandre de Moraes and Dias Toffoli 'rotten fruits'.

item.title: Governo prorroga até 5 de maio prazo para estados aderirem à subvenção ao diesel; 15 já entraram no programa
item.description: The federal government extended until May 5 the deadline for states to join the diesel subsidy program, which provides R$1.20 per liter for imported diesel. Fifteen states have already joined, but the extension aims to overcome resistance from state audit courts claiming prior legislative approval was needed — now clarified as unnecessary by the new decree. The program costs R$4 billion over two months, half funded by the federal government and half by the states, as part of a broader effort to counter fuel price increases driven by the Middle East war.

item.title: Zema diz que votar escala 6x1 em ano eleitoral é populismo e afirma que STF tem três 'frutas podres'
item.description: Romeu Zema (NOVO), a pre-candidate for Presidency, labeled the proposal to end the 6x1 work scale as 'pure populism', advocating for a flexible hourly work model similar to the U.S. He also harshly criticized three Supreme Court ministers, calling them 'rotten fruits' and linking them to scandals like the Banco Master case, without providing evidence. The STF did not respond to the accusations by the time of publication.

item.title: Lula está liberado para tocar a campanha, afirma Roberto Kalil
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, has been cleared by his medical team to resume his re-election campaign after two minor surgical procedures: removal of a scalp keratosis and a wrist injection for right-hand thumb tendinitis. Doctors state there are no restrictions on his schedule, though he should avoid large events in the coming days and wear a bandage and hat for about a month during healing.

item.title: Lula fala em delegados 'fingindo trabalhar' e associação reage com críticas a 'generalização'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Federal Police delegates and agents were 'pretending to work' outside the force and ordered the Justice Minister to recall those not serving as state secretaries, as part of an effort to combat organized crime. The National Association of Federal Police Delegates (ADPF) criticized the remarks as an unfair generalization, noting that 53 delegates assigned to other branches perform strategic functions and that recalling them would not significantly affect organized crime, while also highlighting structural issues such as loss of qualified personnel and declining interest in the career.

item.title: Gilmar conversa com Hugo Motta e irá a Lula e Alcolumbre por pacto entre os Poderes
item.description: Justice Gilmar Mendes, dean of the STF, is leading an inter-power pact for institutional reform, having already spoken with Chamber President Hugo Motta and planning talks with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre and President Lula. The initiative, originally pushed by Flávio Dino and now led by Mendes, seeks to distribute responsibility for judicial improvements beyond the Supreme Court, rejecting Fachin’s isolated conduct code proposal in light of the Banco Master scandal. The argument is that systemic issues — like those tied to Daniel Vorcaro — require collective action, not isolated fixes.

item.title: TSE publica acórdão do julgamento que deixa Cláudio Castro inelegível; ex-governador não foi cassado
item.description: The TSE published the ruling declaring former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro ineligible for abuse of power in the 2022 elections, but confirmed his departure was via resignation, not cassation, preventing mandate loss and leaving the succession model to be defined by the STF or Alerj. Meanwhile, the state government remains under interim leadership of the TJ-RJ president, and Alerj has petitioned the STF for immediate swearing-in of Douglas Ruas as interim governor.

item.title: A retomada das ações afirmativas na gestão pública
item.description: The third Lula government revived affirmative action in public administration through Decree 11.443/2023, setting a minimum 30% target for Black representation in commissioned positions, with measurable progress by 2026. The policy aims to build a representative bureaucracy, addressing preparation, entry, retention, and promotion with monitoring and evaluation. Black representation in high-level positions rose from 25% in 2014 to 36% in 2024, showing consistent gains after years of setbacks.

item.title: A munição que comitês de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro preparam para atirar contra a família do adversário
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are preparing for a 2026 electoral campaign marked by personal attacks on each other's families. While Lula seeks to revive the argument that the country cannot return to the hands of a Bolsonaro, Flávio aims to position himself as an 'improved' version of his father, trying to distance his image from Jair Bolsonaro's controversies. Both sides plan to use scandals involving relatives: the Lula campaign points to alleged links between Lulinha and a lobbyist accused of frauding the INSS, while the Bolsonaros intend to exploit plea bargains to attack the president's family.

item.title: TSE realiza nesta segunda (27) atualizações na infraestrutura de Tecnologia da Informação
item.description: The TSE will perform IT infrastructure updates on Monday, January 27, from 8 a.m. to 12 p.m., aimed at maintaining the database of the Candidacy System (CAND). During this period, the Candidacy and Electoral Time systems will be unavailable. The measure aims to ensure the stability and proper functioning of electoral systems.

item.title: Lula acerta ao adotar reciprocidade contra EUA, mas caso Ramagem não mobiliza como tarifaço a favor do petista
item.description: Lula was right to apply reciprocity against the U.S., revoking credentials of an American military official, but the Ramagem case did not mobilize as much as the 2025 tariff hike. According to Ativaweb DataLab, the tariff episode generated over 5.9 million mentions and national unity, while the current anti-U.S. discourse had 3.1 million mentions, with 77% negative, due to lack of direct economic impact and failure to break ideological bubbles.

item.title: Imposto para quem exporta: a falsa solução do governo Lula
item.description: The Lula government imposed a 12% tax on petroleum exports through Provisional Measure 1.340/2026, aiming to lower domestic fuel prices by compelling producers to sell locally. However, the policy overlooks the adverse effects on national producers, who may cut investments or pass on costs, rendering the solution ineffective and potentially counterproductive.

item.title: Reação de ministro Gilmar turbina Zema e impulsiona engajamento da pauta anti-Supremo
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court’s (STF) reaction to Senator Alessandro Vieira’s request to indict ministers—particularly Justice Gilmar Mendes’ move to include Governor Romeu Zema in the fake news inquiry—has inadvertently amplified political engagement around the anti-Supreme narrative. This response boosted Zema’s visibility and strengthened his confrontation rhetoric, with allies noting recent social media growth. Despite potential reversals, STF justices fear the conflict may become a permanent campaign theme, deepening the Court’s image crisis and prolonging its electoral wear.

item.title: Lula: entenda o que é queratose e tendinite, problemas que motivaram ida do presidente ao hospital
item.description: President Lula was hospitalized to undergo two medical procedures: cauterization to remove a scalp actinic keratosis caused by chronic sun exposure, and a wrist injection to treat tendinitis in the right thumb. Both procedures are outpatient, have quick recovery times, and present no contraindications.

item.title: TSE publicou o acórdão sobre o governo do RJ, mas duas interrogações permanecem
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) published the ruling on the conviction of Cláudio Castro, governor of Rio de Janeiro, stemming from a judgment that took place in March. This publication may unlock the judgment at the Supreme Federal Court (STF) regarding the format of the supplementary election in the state. The article is exclusive to subscribers and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Paes volta a insistir em eleições diretas após acórdão que deixa em aberto escolha de governador para mandato-tampão
item.description: Eduardo Paes (PSD) renewed his call for direct elections in Rio de Janeiro after the TSE's ruling confirmed Claudio Castro's conviction but left the method for filling the interim governorship unresolved. He criticized the state's political leadership since 2019 and emphasized the PSD's legal action at the STF to halt the indirect election and mandate a popular vote, framing the TSE's omission as further justification for 'Diretas Já'.

item.title: Psol pede à PGR anulação de venda de terras-raras em Goiás
item.description: Federal deputies from the Psol party have asked Brazil’s Attorney General’s Office (PGR) to annul the sale of Goiás-based rare earth miner Serra Verde to U.S. company USA Rare Earth for $2.8 billion, citing threats to national economic sovereignty and potential overreach by the state government into federal authority over mining and international relations. The request includes civil and criminal investigations, constitutional review of the state’s actions, and a petition to the STF to nullify all related acts, including contracts, payments, and agreements.

item.title: TSE reconhece renúncia de Cláudio Castro em acórdão de julgamento
item.description: The TSE recognized the resignation of Cláudio Castro in a court ruling, declaring him ineligible for abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections. The decision bars him from running in future elections for eight years.

item.title: Em pleno século 21, Brasil volta aos anos 50 com 'yankees go home' de Lula
item.description: Brazil's Federal Police announced the withdrawal of credentials for a U.S. immigration agent operating in Brazil, framed as retaliation for alleged U.S. actions against Brazilian interests. The incident, occurring on Wednesday the 22nd, was characterized by analysts as a 'yankees go home' political move, evoking historical tensions over national sovereignty. The action reflects Lula’s more assertive foreign policy stance, aligned with narratives of independence and resistance to external pressure.

item.title: Enquanto Flávio Bolsonaro se omite, Zema enfrenta o STF
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, senator and son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, is criticized for his silence amid STF investigations into the so-called 'Coup Plot,' while Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema directly confronts the Supreme Federal Court in judicial matters. Despite his rhetoric of opposing the 'system,' Flávio Bolsonaro did not take a public stance of defiance or confrontation during his father’s testimony, contrasting with Zema’s approach. The piece highlights the inconsistency between Bolsonarist rhetoric of resistance and the practice of silence or evasion under institutional pressure.

item.title: TSE publica acórdão que condena ex-governador Cláudio Castro e confirma renúncia
item.description: The TSE published a ruling confirming the ineligibility of former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro for abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections, but found his cassation moot due to his prior resignation. Rio de Janeiro opted for an indirect election via the state legislature (Alerj) for the interim governorship, and the matter was referred to the STF to determine the selection model, after Justice Flávio Dino requested more time to review the case.

item.title: Lula passa por dois procedimentos médicos no Sírio-Libanês nesta sexta em SP
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva undergoes two medical procedures at São Paulo's Sírio-Libanês Hospital on Friday, the 24th: a scalp cauterization to treat keratosis and an infiltration in his right thumb for tendinitis. The Secretariat of Social Communication (Secom) stated the procedures will not affect his future commitments, and he will remain in São Paulo until Saturday, the 25th, with a planned appearance at the closing of the 8th PT National Congress in Brasília on Sunday, the 26th, pending confirmation the day before.

item.title: Crusoé: O inconfidente
item.description: The article reflects on the commemoration of the Inconfidência Mineira during Tiradentes' holiday, featuring former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema questioning whether Brazilians are truly free today despite historical independence. He links the 18th-century revolt against Portuguese rule to contemporary debates about liberty and governance in Brazil.

item.title: Lula dá entrada em hospital para fazer cauterização na cabeça e infiltração por causa de tendinite na mão
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was admitted to the Albert Einstein Israelite Hospital in São Paulo for a cauterization procedure to remove a scalp keratosis and an injection in his right wrist to treat tendonitis. The procedures are quick and routine, with no contraindications, and Lula is expected to rest at home on Friday and Saturday. His attendance at the PT Congress closing in Brasília on Sunday remains unconfirmed, though he has scheduled engagements in the interior of São Paulo on Monday.

item.title: Uma nota da comunidade para o pedido de desculpas de Gilmar
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes apologized after referencing homosexuality when referring to Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and presidential pre-candidate. The X community issued a note emphasizing that, per STF rulings (ADO 26 and MI 4.733, June 13, 2019), homophobia and transphobia are equated to crime, framing the apology as consistent with existing jurisprudence.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes pede desculpas por citar homossexualidade como possível 'acusação injuriosa' contra Zema: 'Errei'
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes admitted error for citing homosexuality as a possible 'injurious accusation' against Romeu Zema in a TV Globo interview, later apologizing on X. He defended continuing the fake news inquiry and including Zema in the process, citing a 'defamation industry' against the Court. Opposition lawmakers are articulating a new impeachment request against Mendes following his move to include Zema in the investigation.

item.title: Gilmar cita ideia de fazer ‘boneco de Zema como homossexual’ e diz que seria ofensivo
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes suggested in an interview that making dolls of Governor Romeu Zema as homosexual could be considered an injurious accusation, sparking backlash. He later admitted the error, apologized for equating homosexuality with theft, and vowed to confront what he called a 'defamation industry' against the Court. Zema responded that Mendes oversteps boundaries, that comparing homosexuality to theft reveals prejudice, and shared an AI-generated image of himself holding an LGBTQIA+ flag with a laughing emoji.

item.title: O tiro no pé de Gilmar Mendes
item.description: The dean of the Brazilian Supreme Court, Gilmar Mendes, gave a series of unprecedented interviews this week in an attempt to defend the Court’s image and discredit presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema. His effort backfired, drawing criticism and reinforcing perceptions of bias. The episode was described as a 'self-inflicted wound,' as it further damaged the credibility of both Mendes and the STF.

item.title: MEC Livros terá acervo ampliado para 25 mil obras
item.description: The Ministry of Education expanded the MEC Livros collection from 8,000 to 25,000 works and now allows early return of books after reading 10% or 90% of the content, responding to user demand for greater flexibility. The platform, accessible via Gov.br login, has over 500,000 registered users and offers free borrowing of national and international titles. The announcement was made during the 9º Prêmio Vivaleitura, with President Lula in attendance, who emphasized the importance of accessible reading for all.

item.title: Crise entre Zema e o STF escala e ministro já fala em prisão do ex-governador de Minas
item.description: Romeu Zema, presidential candidate for the Novo party, intensified unfounded criticisms of the STF, prompting Minister Gilmar Mendes to act against him in the Fake News inquiry. STF ministers warn that his attacks could lead to legal consequences, including possible imprisonment, though Zema denies crossing any line and defends the right to criticize public officials, even ironically.

item.title: SobeDesce: de John Ternus ao ChatGPT
item.description: Fifty-year-old executive John Ternus will become Apple's new CEO in September, succeeding Tim Cook. Brazilian swimmer Gabriel Araújo was named Paralympic Athlete of the Year at the Laureus World Sports Awards. Meanwhile, ChatGPT is under investigation by Florida's Attorney General for messages exchanged with a shooter who killed two at a university in 2025; Botafogo received a FIFA transfer ban due to debts, and only 36% of Brazilians consider driving electric vehicles.

item.title: Janja e Michelle ganham protagonismo na corrida pelos votos decisivos das mulheres
item.description: Women represent 51.5% of Brazil's population and 52.8% of the electorate, forming a decisive majority in the 2026 elections despite historical exclusion from top political power. Although Lula still maintains above-average approval among women, his support dropped from 48% to 45% between January and April, and his lead over Flávio Bolsonaro in female voters in second-round simulations fell from 13 to 4 points, signaling erosion of his base. The president has intensified agendas like the national pact against femicide to try to reclaim this crucial electorate.

item.title: O atraso
item.description: Lula seeks to improve his electoral image by reviving rhetoric against U.S. tariffs on Brazilian exports, attempting to use a confrontation with Trump as a campaign theme to combat his high rejection. Despite initial diplomatic enthusiasm following brief encounters with Trump, no substantive progress was made in bilateral relations, and Washington officials say nothing has changed. Lula tries to draw Trump into the electoral game, but the relationship remains superficial, based on unmet expectations.

item.title: Caso Ramagem põe governo na mira da oposição e abre outra frente de atrito com Trump
item.description: The swift arrest and release of Alexandre Ramagem in the U.S. exposed flaws in Brazil-U.S. international cooperation, drawing criticism from the U.S. State Department over alleged PF manipulation of immigration systems. The incident allowed Ramagem to retaliate by praising Trump-aligned Bolsonarists in the U.S., calling the PF a 'police of thugs,' and prompting opposition demands for PF director Andrei Rodrigues to testify before the Foreign Relations Committee.

item.title: “O inimigo é o PT”, diz Mateus Simões, governador de Minas
item.description: Governor of Minas Gerais, Mateus Simões (PSD), successor of Romeu Zema, states his goal is to defeat the PT in the 2026 elections, despite trailing in polls. He aims to build a triple ticket with Zema, Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), but emphasizes loyalty to Zema for selecting him as vice. Simões also highlights his strategy of governing outside Belo Horizonte to strengthen his presence in the interior and connect with the state’s political base.

item.title: PT promove 8º congresso de olho em aliança com a “direita liberal”
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) held its 8th National Congress in Brasília, advocating for an alliance with 'liberal right' forces to counter authoritarian far-right movements, strengthen democracy, and expand its political project. The event paid tribute to founding militants Clara Charf and Sonia Braga and discussed proposals including judicial reform, Armed Forces changes, and updates to the party program.

item.title: PL quer confirmar André do Prado como candidato ao Senado por SP em até 10 dias
item.description: The PL is expected to confirm André do Prado as its Senate candidate for São Paulo within 10 days, with support from Governor Tarcísio de Freitas and approval from Eduardo Bolsonaro following a positive meeting in the U.S. The move aims to finalize the state’s majoritarian ticket alongside Tarcísio, positioning André as a moderate figure to balance the bolsonarist alliance.

item.title: Conselheiro de Trump diz que “brasileiras causam confusão”
item.description: Paolo Zampolli, an advisor to Donald Trump, made offensive remarks about Brazilian women in an Rai interview, claiming they are 'programmed to cause confusion' and referring to his ex-wife Amanda Ungaro and a friend named Lídia with derogatory terms. He also had ties to Jeffrey Epstein and proposed replacing Iran with Italy in the 2026 World Cup. Amanda Ungaro, a Brazilian former model, was deported from the U.S. in 2025 and attributes her removal to Zampolli’s political influence.

item.title: Um terço dos partidos pode ficar sem fundo partidário se repetir desempenho de 2022
item.description: At least 11 of Brazil’s 30 political parties could lose access to the Party Fund and free TV/radio advertising in 2026 if they repeat their 2022 performance, due to a stricter electoral barrier clause. Avante, currently eligible, would be excluded, while the PDT narrowly cleared the threshold. To qualify in 2026, parties must secure 2.5% of national valid votes (with 1.5% in nine states or eight plus DF) or elect at least 13 deputies across nine states (or eight plus DF).

item.title: Lula vai retirar queratose na cabeça; entenda o que é o procedimento
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will undergo two simple surgical procedures this Friday at the Sírio-Libanês Hospital: a wrist infiltration to treat thumb tendinitis and removal of a scalp keratosis. Keratosis is a benign skin lesion common in older adults, often removed for aesthetic or preventive reasons, as some types have pre-cancerous potential. The Presidency stated Lula will face no restrictions or need for rest after the procedures.
